## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 20 user-facing changes.
### New
- On Mac, drag a pinned extension along the sidebar to put your extensions in the order you want, as you move tabs. Every Space with the same browsing profile shows them in that order. From the first launch after updating, the strip shows your extensions in the order you pinned them instead of by name. - On Mac, Command-E opens your extensions one at a time: the pinned ones from left to right, then the rest. Press it again for the next one, and once more after the last to close it. Archive Tab moves to Shift-Command-E. - On Mac, you can put the address bar on top: choose Top under Address bar in Settings › Appearance, and the address field with back, forward and reload moves above the page. - On Mac, each page in Split View carries its own bar with back, forward, its address, Site Controls and pinned extensions, wherever the address bar is.
### Improved
- Remove from Folder and Remove from Group put the tab just below its folder or group instead of at the end of your open tabs. - On Mac, pages slide and resize into place as they join or leave Split View instead of jumping.
### Fixed
- A tab you put in a folder on one device no longer disappears from every device when the folder is deleted on another at the same time. It stays with your open tabs. - On Mac, Crest no longer quits while it prepares an import from Arc or another browser when some of that browser's data is damaged. - On Mac, when Crest can't prepare an import from another browser, the review now shows an error with Back and Skip instead of quitting. - Importing from Arc keeps the names you gave tabs there, and the import review shows them. Clearing a name shows the page's title again. - On Mac, Command-W closes every tab you selected in the sidebar again, and Command-D duplicates them, instead of acting on the tab on screen. - On Mac, a folder's … button no longer covers the end of its name when you point at it. The name fades out beneath the button.

## Highlights
### Fixed
- Chromium is updated to 157.0.8103.51, which fixes CVE-2026-125350, a security flaw being exploited in the wild, and eight other security flaws.
---
Stable releases are signed, notarized, and ready for everyday use.

## Highlights
### New
- A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.
### Improved
- Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.
### Fixed
- Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit. - A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs. - A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open. - Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share. - Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder. - Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.
